title: Superconductivity on the verge of metal-insulator transition in Cu$_{1-x}$Zn$_x$Ir$_2$S$_4$ probed by $μ$SR
authors: K. M. Kojima, M. Miyazaki, M. Hiraishi, A. Koda, R. Kadono, C. Baines, Y. Tsuchiya, H. S. Suzuki, H. Kitazawa
abstract: The thiospinel CuIr$_2$S$_4$ undergoes a metal-insulator transition below $\approx$230 K, which is suppressed by substitution of Cu with Zn (Cu$_{1-x}$Zn$_x$Ir$_2$S$_4$) to induce superconductivity for $0.2\lesssim x\lesssim0.8$. We show that the temperature/field dependence of superfluid density in samples with $x = 0.3$ and 0.4 ($T_{\rm c} \approx 3$ K and 2.5 K) investigated by muon spin rotation and relaxation ($μ$SR) is consistent with a fully gapped $s$-wave pairing. Meanwhile, the relatively high resistivity (10$^{-3}$-10$^{-2}$ $Ω\:$cm) in their normal state suggests that the superconductivity is in the "dirty limit" where the mean free path is much shorter than the coherence length ($\ell \ll ξ_0$). This indicates that the potential anisotropy associated with unconventional pairing mechanisms expected under the strong electron correlations is smeared out by the electron scattering. Based on these observations, we discuss potential link between the Zn substitution-induced superconductivity and that recently discovered in CuIr$_2$S$_4$ under high pressure ($>18$ GPa) where the existence of strong electron scattering is also suggested.
summary: This work uses muon spin rotation ($\mu$SR) to study superconductivity in $	ext{Cu}_{1-x}	ext{Zn}_x	ext{Ir}_2	ext{S}_4$, a material near a metal-insulator transition. The results confirm an s-wave superconducting state, arguing that high electronic disorder forces the pairing symmetry into an isotropic form. This suggests that structural scattering and proximity to the Mott-Ioffe-Regel limit are key tuners of superconductivity in this correlated system.
main_problem: Investigating superconductivity in Zn-substituted thiospinel $	ext{Cu}_{1-x}	ext{Zn}_x	ext{Ir}_2	ext{S}_4$ near a metal-insulator transition to understand the pairing mechanism.
main_result: The superconducting state is confirmed to be an isotropic, fully gapped s-wave symmetry, which is robustly maintained deep within the 'dirty limit' due to strong electron scattering.
method: Transverse-field muon spin rotation ($\mu$SR) measurements were used to probe the temperature and field dependence of the superfluid density.
model_or_system: The system is the thiospinel $	ext{CuIr}_2	ext{S}_4$, whose superconducting properties are tuned by Zn substitution ($x$), driving it away from a high-temperature metal-insulator transition. The analysis compares results to models incorporating disorder and pressure effects.
key_observables: Superfluid density ($\sigma_s$) derived from $\mu$SR linewidth, normal state resistivity ($ho$), magnetic susceptibility, and the superconducting critical temperature ($T_c$).
important_parameters: The system operates in the 'dirty limit' ($\ell \ll \xi_0$) and near the Mott-Ioffe-Regel (MIR) limit due to structural disorder/frustration.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes a Gaussian approximation for field distributions in $\mu$SR fitting, and that high scattering averages out potential gap anisotropy.
figures_summary: Figures show the temperature dependence of the $\mu$SR linewidth ($\sigma$) below $T_c$, confirming superconducting transitions, alongside magnetic susceptibility data showing order parameter development.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the background on the MI transition and Zn-induced superconductivity. It presents $\mu$SR results showing s-wave pairing in the dirty limit, arguing that disorder smears out unconventional signatures. Finally, it proposes a unified framework linking electronic disorder, proximity to the MIR limit, and high pressure effects.
why_interesting: The paper provides experimental evidence of how strong scattering (disorder) can stabilize an isotropic s-wave superconducting state even when underlying physics suggests complex, anisotropic pairing mechanisms expected in correlated materials.
